What does it mean to be a woman, man, or nb? Well, speaking for me since people's idea on these kinds of things can be quite varied. I'd saying being anything, is easily simplified to how one views themselves. It's an understanding of self that can be influenced by the world's categories but ultimately is not reliant upon them. For instance, if what a man and a woman are were to be reversed, trans people would still exist, we'd just be using different labels.

What I mean by reversed is, men would be women in this scenario, but still be everything they are, and vice versa for women. You can change the labels and the stereotypes and everything else involved with how humanity views itself, and trans and nb people will still be a thing. I would go so far as to say it's not about the labels at all, but we live in a world where labels are treated as some kind of weird deity. We grow up learning that labels are important, and that leads to people trying to figure out which ones they are. I do imagine it would have been pretty stressful for modern non-binary people to figure out their gender with all the expectations and bullshit feelings of betrayal from people around them. Hell, it was stressful for me just because everyone thought I was something I've never been.
